entry.title: Anode-free sodium batteries last longer thanks to an electrolyte that forms its own shield
entry.summary: Sodium batteries, which store and release electrical energy by moving sodium ions between their two electrodes, could be a more affordable alternative to lithium-based batteries. This is because sodium is highly abundant on Earth and can be sourced from widely available raw materials.

entry.title: Taming blue light: Researchers bring precision lasers onto a chip
entry.summary: Blue lasers are already widely available. But making their light extremely stable while also changing its frequency at high speed is a much harder challenge, and one that has limited the development of compact, high-performance laser systems.

entry.title: Scientists turn Moon dust into LEGO-like bricks for future lunar bases
entry.summary: Scientists have found a way to 3D-print Moon dust into LEGO-like bricks, raising the possibility of building lunar bases using materials already on the Moon. The experimental blocks still need to be strengthened, but the technology could transform how humans construct permanent settlements beyond Earth.

entry.title: CERN scientists finally find evidence of a particle decay so rare it took 40 years to detect
entry.summary: Scientists at CERN have found the first evidence of an incredibly rare particle decay after more than 40 years of searching, detecting a process expected to occur just once in every 10 billion beauty particles. The breakthrough could help physicists explore a mysterious microscopic realm where unknown particles and forces may be hiding.

entry.title: Two massive stars may be secretly feeding the Milky Way’s supermassive black hole
entry.summary: Astronomers have traced mysterious gas clouds near the Milky Way's central supermassive black hole to a massive pair of stars whose colliding winds appear to create dense clumps of material. These clouds may eventually feed the black hole, revealing a surprising connection between stellar activity and the growth of cosmic giants.
